coachMessages.text: Green always goes first. In any empty column, who lands on the bottom cell? Who lands one above? Follow the sequence.

slides.infoProse:
Green plays first, so the first disc in any empty column always belongs to Green — that is row 0 (0-indexed, bottom). Gray lands at row 1, Green at row 2, Gray at row 3, and so on. The pattern never breaks.

Green owns rows 1, 3, 5 (odd numbers)

coachMessages.text: Each column runs its own alternation independently. Count the discs already in the column — that tells you who owns the next cell.

slides.infoProse: Each column has its own mini-game. Count how many discs are already there — the next disc in that column belongs to whoever is next in the alternation for that column's current height. The global rule (Green first everywhere) means: if a column has an even number of discs (0, 2, 4…), the next disc is Green's; if it has an odd number (1, 3, 5…), the next disc is Gray's.

coachMessages.text: Watch out: the same row number can belong to different players in different columns. The row alone doesn't tell you who owns it.

slides.infoProse:
This is the critical trap: the same row number belongs to different players in different columns, depending on how many discs are already there. Row 3 in a fresh column belongs to Green (it is the 3rd disc, Green's turn). Row 3 in a column that already has one disc belongs to Gray (it is the 2nd disc to be placed, Gray's turn).

The shortcut: **subtract the current column height from the row number.** If the result is even, Green owns it; if odd, Gray owns it.

coachMessages.text: A threat is only real if the right player lands on the completing cell. Who will get there first in this column?

slides.infoProse: A threat is only as good as who lands on the completing cell. Before trusting any threat, ask: will I actually reach that cell, or will my opponent get there first? This is the question that Claimeven, Z-Threats, and all parity-based strategies are built on — and it all comes back to this one rule: count from the current column height.
